game.title: Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit
game.blurb: Arcade racing game from Electronic Arts and Criterion Games, published by Electronic Arts, released 2010-11-16. RAWG average playtime: 3 hours. Genres: Racing, Arcade. Chapters follow the modes the achievement list on RAWG shows: the Racer and Cop careers, online, Autolog, car challenges, the named event packs and pursuit tech.

chapters.title: Racer Career
chapters.summary: Climbing the Racer wanted levels, gold medals in every single-player Racer event, and named Racer events.

chapters.title: Cop Career
chapters.summary: Climbing the Cop ranks, a Distinction in every single-player Cop mission, and Hot Pursuit, Interceptor and Rapid Response events.

chapters.title: Online Modes
chapters.summary: Online Races, Hot Pursuit, Interceptor, Most Wanted and Arms Race, as a Racer and as a Cop. Needs a network connection, if the servers still run.

chapters.title: Autolog, Friends and Dreamshots
chapters.summary: NFS Friends, Autolog recommendations, posts on the Wall, and taking and sharing Dreamshots and pictures.

chapters.title: Car Challenges
chapters.summary: Feats in named cars: top speeds, drifts, nitrous, long drives, wrecks and busts in a particular car.

chapters.title: Super Sports, Porsche Pack and Lamborghini Pack
chapters.summary: Medals in the Super Sports Racer and Cop events and the Porsche Pack and Lamborghini Pack events the achievements name.

chapters.title: Pursuit Tech and Driving
chapters.summary: Spike strips, EMPs, road blocks, helicopters and jammers, busting and wrecking, and nitrous and turbo runs.

notes: Backlog game, all-AAA pass: picked from RAWG's most-added list for its year across all genres (docs/PLAN.md section 2, genre filter widened 2026-10-23). RAWG's first result is the expected entry (need-for-speed-hot-pursuit-2, id 19633, released 2010-11-16); "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2" (2002), "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered" (2020) and "Need for Speed 3: Hot Pursuit" (1998) are other entries and were not used. The only Steam store-list match is "Need for Speed™ Hot Pursuit Remastered" (app 1328660), a different product, so it was not used; RAWG's Steam link for this entry gives app 47870, whose schema is empty, so steam=None. RAWG lists "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered" and "Need for Speed Hot Pursuit for iPad" as additions. StrategyWiki has no page under "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010)"; the guide is under "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit" (categories 2010, 2020 and Criterion Games), at completion stage 1. Its written pages are Cars (PC, Consoles) (about 19,500 characters), Achievements and trophies (about 11,800), Cars availability (about 10,000), DLC (about 9,400), Equipment (about 8,800), Gameplay (about 4,600), Controls, Walkthrough (about 2,100), Nitrous, Cars (mobile) and Table of Contents; there are no event or chapter pages, so it was not used. nfs.fandom.com answers the API under "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010)" with about 160 linked articles; its subpage names (Career/Racer, Career/SCPD, Hot Pursuit, Interceptor, Rapid Response, Most Wanted, Arms Race, Race, Autolog, Downloadable Content) match the modes the achievements name. Names only were looked at, nothing copied. Whether the Super Sports, Porsche Pack and Lamborghini Pack events are paid add-ons is not in the data we used.
